title: Audit Argus documentation against current contracts and production
Harden containerized PostgreSQL recovery operations
body:
## Summary

This hardens Argus's shared PostgreSQL backup and restore workflow for the homelab production topology.

The retention false-negative was caused by opening the live PostgreSQL data directory with strict no-atime/read requirements. The homelab operator does not own the container-owned PGDATA directory (host UID 999), so a read-only retention scan could fail before it ever evaluated the backup snapshots. The live path is a boundary check only; this change validates its metadata without changing ownership or reading its contents.

## Changes

- Make retention validation metadata-only for the live PostgreSQL data directory while retaining descriptor-bound strict reads for backup snapshots and marker files.
- Add container-aware backup streaming through `docker exec` for `pg_dump`, `pg_dumpall`, and archive validation.
- Add container-aware isolated restore using disposable databases and `docker exec`.
- Add an explicit `--skip-migration` path only for container restores whose dump is then fully verified at the current schema head.
- Add regression and static contract tests for the container path and metadata-only retention behavior.

## Verification

Local focused verification:

```
43 passed, 16 skipped, 2 deselected
```

Also passed:

- `git diff --check`
- shell syntax checks for both PostgreSQL scripts
- Python bytecode compilation for the recovery modules

Live homelab evidence, performed before publication:

- backup set `20260725T205751Z` created successfully
- both custom-format database archives and globals passed structural validation and checksums
- isolated Argus and Atlas restore completed successfully
- restored schema head: `0006_maya_outbox`
- all recovery checks passed
- fresh promotion gate: `allowed: true`
- scratch restore databases were removed
- no PostgreSQL filesystem ownership change was made
- actual retention deletion/reclamation remains disabled

The provider/API/MCP runtime smoke checks are also green on homelab; this PR is limited to recovery hardening and does not change provider enablement.

title: Wayfinder: make Argus stable and competitively optimized without a rewrite
body:
## Destination

A decision-complete, low-rewrite handoff for making Argus stable, measurably competitive, and operationally complete on the private homelab. The destination is one production execution authority with truthful PostgreSQL/recovery/provider evidence, immutable release and rollback proof, current documentation, and independently testable retrieval/extraction improvements ported mechanically after design.

## Notes

- This issue is the coordination map, not the implementation workspace. Child issues are claimed and resolved one at a time.
- The closure authority is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-retrieval-evidence-mechanical-port.md`, including its revised closure-driven critical path and terminal-state protocol.
- Production actions remain evidence-backed and reversible. Preserve dirty homelab worktrees; do not perform destructive deletion, secret rotation, credit purchases, irreversible migrations, promotion, or deployment without the explicit gate named by the plan.
- Runtime, migrations, cutover, and rollback proof run on the homelab. The Mac is for source editing, hermetic tests, Git, GitHub, and read-only inspection.
- The map remains bounded: no mandatory runtime LLM planner, vector-database migration, broad rewrite, unbounded paid polling, duplicate ticket creation, or manual benchmark/research queue for the owner.
- At most one successor implementation issue and PR may be open at a time. Each predecessor must be terminal on `main` before the next is created.

## Decisions so far

- Stability and truthful measurement come first; development stays isolated from production until the scorecard and contract gates are complete.
- The budgeted profile may use available providers within policy; `--free` and `free_only=true` permit recurring free quota and eligible cached evidence but initiate no new billable provider call.
- Retrieval optimization uses bounded planning, provider-aware signals, provenance/evidence envelopes, cache/latency discipline, and truthful health/budget states.
- HTTP is the production execution authority and MCP is a stateless caller adapter.
- PostgreSQL is the intended production authority; the temporary atlas-postgres name must give way to canonical homelab-postgres without breaking Atlas compatibility.
- [Run Argus on shared homelab PostgreSQL with verified recovery](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/40) — PostgreSQL is the live authority through canonical `homelab-postgres`, with durable least-privilege configuration and verified backup, restore, recovery, HTTP, persistence, and MCP evidence.
- [Define the Argus stability and competitive evidence scorecard](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/59) — stability is an absolute automated gate, while competitive promotion requires reproducible evidence-package improvement over a frozen baseline without manual benchmark labor.
- [Implement S0 accepted-operation contract kernel and frozen fixtures](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/82) — canonical outcomes and frozen compatibility fixtures are merged.
- [Implement S1 deterministic retrieval plan and identities](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/84) — bounded deterministic planning and cache identities are merged.
- [Implement S2 provider batch normalization and private failure evidence](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/86) — provider evidence is normalized behind a private bounded envelope.
- [Implement S3 extraction finalization and retrieval composition](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/88) — extraction outcomes finalize once with explicit rejection evidence.
- [Implement S4 exact provider-aware evidence fusion](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/90) — freshness, duplicate, provenance, diversity, and rank fusion are deterministic.
- [Implement S5 provider readiness as the sole decision authority](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/92) — readiness and spend decisions are centralized and fail closed.
- [Implement S6 accepted retrieval, durable evidence, and immutable cache](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/94) — accepted retrieval, schema head 0009, PostgreSQL evidence, and immutable cache publication are merged.
- [Implement consolidated HTTP accepted-operation authority and secure v2 transport](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/97) — one accepted-operation authority now preserves frozen v1 behavior, exposes exact secure v2 HTTP contracts, and binds planning through durable acceptance without duplicate execution.
- [Implement negotiated MCP and CLI client transports](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/99) — MCP and CLI now negotiate capabilities without speculative fallback, preserve frozen legacy behavior, and enforce secure versioned transport semantics.
- [Implement workflow extraction composition and delivery safety](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/101) — accepted workflow extraction now persists receipt-bound total links, resumes idempotently, and blocks rejected or diagnostic-only content from synthesis and delivery.

## Not yet specified

No implementation fog remains. [Implement hermetic scorecard and immutable candidate evidence bundle](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/103) is the active frontier. After it is terminal on `main`, protected P1 promotion closes [Promote immutable homelab releases with rollback proof](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/41), then [Cut over private homelab production and retire duplicate authorities](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/42), then [Publish the Argus production operations and recovery runbook](https://github.com/Khamel83/argus/issues/44). This map closes last.

## Out of scope

- Mandatory runtime model-backed planning, vector search, broad rewrites, provider-credit top-ups, and destructive automatic retention deletion.
- Treating a stale SQLite artifact as a second authority; its archival/removal is a separate explicitly gated cleanup action.

title: Persist structured extraction rejection reasons for Atlas callers
body:
## Problem

Atlas preserved terminal URL/capture failures from the recovery window, but the persisted error text is too generic to distinguish why Argus output was rejected. Later live re-tests showed at least one diagnostic target extracted cleanly, which means the historical Atlas failure was likely transient or environment-related, but the durable record did not retain enough structured detail to prove that directly.

This is not a request to replay old Atlas failures or rerun user-owned public-extraction waves. It is an Argus observability improvement for future Atlas callers.

## Privacy-safe evidence

- Atlas currently has zero eligible capture/URL work, so this is not an active drain blocker.
- Argus and Argus MCP are currently healthy in production.
- A historical Atlas capture failure used a generic message equivalent to "Argus did not return complete content".
- A later live Argus check against the same kind of diagnostic target returned complete usable extraction, so the old generic message was insufficient to determine whether the original failure was quality-gate rejection, incomplete extraction, provider unreachability, timeout, restart churn, or another transient condition.
- Atlas recovery rules require preserving terminal evidence and avoiding blind replay of failed public-extraction waves.

No private URLs, content IDs, titles, tokens, or source content are included here.

## Impact on Atlas

- Future Atlas audits cannot reliably separate persistent Argus extraction defects from transient provider/container failures using the saved error alone.
- Operators may need to perform fresh live re-tests to classify old failures, which is slower and can be misleading if the provider has recovered.
- Generic errors make it harder for Atlas to decide whether a failure should remain terminal, be quarantined, or be eligible for a future explicitly approved retry workflow.

## Proposed behavior

When Argus rejects or downgrades an extraction result for a caller, persist a small structured, privacy-safe rejection object alongside the response, for example:

- `rejection_code`: stable enum such as `quality_gate_failed`, `incomplete_content`, `provider_unavailable`, `timeout`, `parse_error`, `unsupported_source`, `rate_limited`, `empty_result`
- `provider`: provider/adapter name only, not URL or content
- `quality_passed`: boolean or null
- `is_complete`: boolean or null
- `recommended_action`: stable enum such as `retry_later`, `terminal`, `fallback_provider`, `manual_review`
- `attempt_count` and bounded timing/status metadata where available

## Acceptance criteria

- Argus API responses expose a privacy-safe structured rejection reason whenever extraction is not accepted as usable.
- Argus logs and/or persisted request records retain the same rejection code without raw URLs, tokens, titles, or extracted content.
- Atlas callers can store the rejection code verbatim and show aggregate counts by reason.
- Existing successful extraction responses remain unchanged except for optional diagnostic metadata.
- Tests cover at least: incomplete content, quality gate failure, provider unavailable/timeout, and successful extraction.
- Documentation explains that this does not authorize replaying historical Atlas failures; it only improves future evidence quality.

title: Make HTTP the sole production execution authority
body:
Closes #37

## Summary
- make authenticated HTTP the only production owner of broker, provider, extraction, PostgreSQL, budget, health, session, and outbox execution
- turn MCP into a stateless HTTP adapter with end-to-end bearer identity propagation and explicit development-only standalone compatibility
- route production CLI operations through HTTP and fail closed for direct broker, extraction, worker, and cookie execution
